players.product: DDR5 RCD / MRDIMM register & power chipsets, SOCAMM2, memory-interface silicon IP

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO): revenue for the fourth quarter was $190.2 million, above expectations; product revenue was $96.8 million, another quarter of record product revenue, representing 32% year-over-year growth driven by continued strength in DDR5 products and ramping new product contributions; contract and other revenue was $21.8 million, predominantly Silicon IP; operating expenses of $64.9 million were flat compared to Q3; non-GAAP net income was $74.7 million. Record cash from operations of $99.8 million; free cash flow was $91.2 million in the quarter and $320.9 million for the full year (a 45% free cash flow margin); cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $761.8 million. 2025 cash from operations was a company record $360 million, up 56% from 2024. CEO: 'We closed with a strong Q4, with record revenue and earnings.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $190.2 million; record product revenue $96.8 million (32% YoY); contract and other revenue $21.8 million; FY2025 free cash flow $320.9 million (45% margin)

quarterly_data.signal: ONE-TIME SUPPLY CHAIN ISSUE HITS Q1 2026 (CEO): in Q4 Rambus identified a back-end manufacturing issue with one of its OSATs (not named), affecting 'an extremely low number of parts'; the root cause was identified and corrective actions implemented with supply chain partners. Rambus pulled forward fresh material from inventory originally staged for Q1 to meet strong Q4 customer demand, and out of an abundance of precaution quarantined all potentially impacted production material, which is being retested with enhanced screens; this put additional strain on capacity and created a tighter supply environment that affects Q1. Only the RCD was affected; the companion chips were not affected at all. CFO: the Q1 impact would probably have been 'around a low double-digit million impact' in an already seasonally soft quarter; inventory is expected to be replenished by the end of Q1 to support Q2 2026 demand. Management: no reputational harm with customers; the product business is expected to return to strong growth in Q2 and 2026 product revenue remains on track to grow faster than the market.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue impact around a low double-digit million (RCD only)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 non-GAAP outlook (CFO): revenue guided from $172 million at the low end (the transcript prints the range as 'between $172 million and $108 million'); non-GAAP operating profit between $68 million and $78 million; $6 million of interest income; Q1 capital expenditures approximately $13 million; 2026 pro forma tax rate of 16%, driven by tax legislation changes last year; 110 million diluted shares; non-GAAP EPS between $0.56 and $0.64. Q1 product revenue is impacted by the supply chain issue, with resumption of growth expected from the second quarter onwards. Gross margin: 2025 gross margins were around 61.5%, in line with 2024 and consistent with the 60% to 65% long-term model; the business has operated in a tight 61 to 63% range over the last three years, which the CFO called a fair way to think about 2026, with continued pricing discipline and manufacturing cost savings.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue guide from $172 million (upper bound garbled in transcript); non-GAAP operating profit $68 million-$78 million; non-GAAP EPS $0.56-$0.64; Q1 capex approximately $13 million; 2025 gross margin around 61.5%

quarterly_data.signal: DDR5 RCD SHARE AND GENERATION MIX (CEO): Rambus believes it ended 2025 at mid-40% share for DDR5 RCDs, up from the early forties in 2024, the result of a larger design-win footprint at every DDR5 generation; the market grew mid-single digit from 2024 to 2025 while the DDR5 portion rose and DDR4 kept shrinking. DDR5 is still early in its cycle, leaving room to gain share: 'We always said we could be between forty and fifty.' Mix: in Q4 Gen 2 was predominant and Gen 3 was starting to ramp (growing vs Q3); in 2026 Gen 3 is expected to be the predominant version of DDR5; Gen 4 will contribute but with more limited adoption because it is on a different type of core; the big next step is Gen 5, which depends on the introduction of next-generation Intel and AMD platforms. As DIMM speeds rise, customers increasingly want all module chips from the same supplier for interoperability, an indirect positive for Rambus's companion chips.
quarterly_data.figure: mid-40% DDR5 RCD share in 2025 (early forties in 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: NEW PRODUCTS / COMPANION CHIPS (CFO): new products grew from low single-digit contribution in 2025 to upper single digits of product revenue in Q4, in line with expectations, and are expected to grow to about double-digit contribution of total product revenue in Q1; PMIC remains the largest contributor, with customers valuing the interplay between RCD and PMIC, and volume shipments are underway. CEO: growing adoption of DDR5 PMICs contributed to 2025 revenue growth; Rambus introduced a complete client chipset and now offers a chipset portfolio supporting all JEDEC standard DDR5 and LPDDR5 modules across server and client systems. The client market remains minimal for Rambus because clock (CKD) chip adoption is limited to the very high end of the client space, and it will still be minimal in 2026; the long-run goal is 20% share there; the vast majority of the business is in the data center.
quarterly_data.figure: new products upper single digits of product revenue in Q4, about double-digit in Q1 2026; long-run client share goal 20%

quarterly_data.signal: MRDIMM AND SOCAMM2 TIMING (CEO): MRDIMM timing unchanged; the rollout depends on the Intel and AMD platform rollouts (the analyst cited Intel Diamond Rapids and AMD Venice). Rambus expects MRDIMM to ramp towards the very end of 2026, with only the very initial contribution towards the end of the year and the main contribution happening in 2027: 'As far as we're concerned, we are ready.' SOCAMM2: 'On SOCAM two, we have an opportunity for the SPD hub'; Rambus is taking part in defining next-generation SOCAMM chips, where power management could open further opportunities, in line with its strategy of having solutions for every JEDEC standard module on the client and data center side.

SERVER MARKET BASIS AND SUPPLY CONSTRAINTS (CEO): Gartner is at 8% server growth and other sources say double-digit, but Rambus stays prudent and uses mid to high single-digit growth for the server market as its basis, because some tend to underestimate potential shortages, especially on the memory side; Rambus expects to grow faster than that on rising channel counts, new platforms and its new products. Customers say server demand is solid (the refresh cycle is not over, plus agentic AI and inference applications) but that they will be constrained by supply, and lead times continue to lengthen on the supply side: 'in 2026, the demand is solid. But we're going to be more constrained by supply than we're going to be by demand.' Agentic AI is catalyzing traditional CPU-based server demand and the need for more DIMMs per system; the average number of DIMMs per channel keeps growing but is hard to quantify, and the memory market overall is expected to be constrained.
quarterly_data.figure: server market basis mid to high single-digit growth (Gartner is at 8%)

quarterly_data.signal: SILICON IP (CEO/CFO): increasing design wins and customer engagement led by Rambus's latest-generation HBM4, GDDR7 and PCIe7 digital IP plus its security IP; the increasing pace and diversity of AI chip designs, including custom silicon for hyperscalers, is driving wins for high-speed memory interconnect and security IP, with growing demand for interface and security IP to move and secure data in scale-up and scale-out. Customers increasingly run one-year product cadences. Rambus targets companies developing their own accelerators, inference chips and processors with a laser-focused portfolio (PCIe, CXL, HBM, GDDR and security IP) that can support a large number of customers. Asked whether chip design starts are slowing, the CFO said silicon IP performed in line with expectations in 2025 and is expected to continue to grow in 2026 in line with long-term growth expectations.
